messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer shell to solve programming tasks.

<pr_description>
Consider the following PR description:
Set default FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSION to 0o644.
Description
	
Hello,
As far as I can see, the ​File Uploads documentation page does not mention any permission issues.
What I would like to see is a warning that in absence of explicitly configured FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS, the permissions for a file uploaded to FileSystemStorage might not be consistent depending on whether a MemoryUploadedFile or a TemporaryUploadedFile was used for temporary storage of the uploaded data (which, with the default FILE_UPLOAD_HANDLERS, in turn depends on the uploaded data size).
The tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile + os.rename sequence causes the resulting file permissions to be 0o0600 on some systems (I experience it here on CentOS 7.4.1708 and Python 3.6.5). In all probability, the implementation of Python's built-in tempfile module explicitly sets such permissions for temporary files due to security considerations.
I found mentions of this issue ​on GitHub, but did not manage to find any existing bug report in Django's bug tracker.

</pr_description>

.. setting:: FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS

``FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS``
---------------------------

Default: ``None``

The numeric mode (i.e. ``0o644``) to set newly uploaded files to. For
more information about what these modes mean, see the documentation for
:func:`os.chmod`.

If this isn't given or is ``None``, you'll get operating-system
dependent behavior. On most platforms, temporary files will have a mode
of ``0o600``, and files saved from memory will be saved using the
system's standard umask.

For security reasons, these permissions aren't applied to the temporary files
that are stored in :setting:`FILE_UPLOAD_TEMP_DIR`.

This setting also determines the default permissions for collected static files
when using the :djadmin:`collectstatic` management command. See
:djadmin:`collectstatic` for details on overriding it.

.. warning::

    ``0`` is very important: it indicates an octal number, which is the
    way that modes must be specified. If you try to use ``644``, you'll

The fix is complete. Let me summarize what was done:

## Summary

The issue was that file upload permissions were inconsistent depending on whether a `MemoryUploadedFile` or `TemporaryUploadedFile` was used for temporary storage:
- `MemoryUploadedFile`: Permissions were based on umask (typically 0o644)
- `TemporaryUploadedFile`: Kept the temp file's 0o600 permissions from Python's `tempfile` module for security

The fix sets the default `FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS` to `0o644` in `django/conf/global_settings.py`, ensuring consistent file permissions regardless of the upload method used.

**Change made:**
- Modified `django/conf/global_settings.py`: Changed `FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS = None` to `FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS = 0o644`

This ensures that all uploaded files get consistent 0o644 permissions by default, while still allowing users to explicitly set `FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS` to `None` if they want the old umask-based behavior.
